steps.prompt: Replace the teddy bear in this puppet parts sheet with Axel the axolotl: a friendly purple axolotl with soft lilac skin, a pale cream belly, three feathery magenta gills on each side of the head, big round black eyes, a wide gentle smile, and a small teal dungaree. This is a body-parts breakout sheet, and its layout is fixed: keep every one of the ten parts in its exact position, at its exact size, on the same flat uniform mid-grey ground. Top row — the head on the left, the torso on the right. Middle row, left to right — left upper arm, left lower arm with its hand, right lower arm with its hand, right upper arm. Bottom row, left to right — left upper leg, left lower leg with its foot, right upper leg, right lower leg with its foot. Each part is a separate floating piece with clear empty grey all around it: no part touches, overlaps or casts a shadow onto another, nothing is added between them, and no part is moved, resized, merged or left out. Draw each limb segment straight and upright, the way it sits in the relaxed symmetrical A-pose the assembled puppet stands in, with rounded ends and a generous cap at the joint so the seam hides when the limb bends. Keep the character identical across all ten pieces — one palette, one fur or skin texture, one costume — and keep the face front-facing and friendly. Flat solid uniform grey background, no gradient, no texture, no drop shadows, no grid lines, no labels, no text. Bright, soft 3D cartoon style with rounded, simplified forms and cheerful proportions. Saturated colors, smooth shading, soft highlights, toy-like glossy finish. Premium preschool learning app asset, no text, no letters, no words.
